- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.0), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3), model often underestimates or lags behind true price rise; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to catch momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (true > 85), model frequently overcorrects or underreacts; add a 1–2 day lag adjustment to avoid overshoot.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend in forecast vs true, model may be too aggressive; apply a 0.3–0.7% downward bias to next period.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) prices; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for days 25–30 if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated +0.30 or higher, model tends to overreact; apply a 0.5–1.0% dampening factor to avoid overcorrection.
